basic_identification.full_title: Aluminium Alloy Forging Stock and Forgings (Alloy 24345) for Aerospace Applications — Specification (First Revision)

scope.summary: This standard covers the metallurgical and physical requirements of aluminium-copper-magnesium-silicon-manganese alloy (Alloy 24345) forging stocks (including billets, bars, rods, and sections) and forgings. The material is intended primarily for aircraft structural parts and components requiring moderate strength and high structural reliability.

revision_history.edition: First Revision (reorganized to rationalize the chemical composition and mechanical properties to align with international aerospace specifications and indigenous manufacturing practices)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all notified aluminium products—including alloy forging stocks and hand/die forgings for structural applications—must comply with the applicable standard and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or selling non-certified structural alloy stocks is a statutory offense. Export-oriented fabrications conforming to foreign buyers' specifications are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to aircraft structural alloy billets and forgings.

requirements.detail: Each package or consignment of forging stock or forgings conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The forging alloy represents Al-Cu-Mg-Si-Mn composition (Alloy 24345) and must strictly meet chemical requirements: Aluminium (Remainder), Copper (3.9 to 5.0%), Silicon (0.5 to 1.2%), Manganese (0.4 to 1.2%), and Magnesium (0.2 to 0.8%).
Forging stock and forgings must be of uniform quality, sound, and entirely free from harmful structural or visual defects such as cracks, voids, laps, seams, folds, or non-metallic inclusions.
The forgings are typical solution heat-treated and precipitation-hardened (artificial aging) to develop optimal metallurgical strength and fatigue properties.

Extruded forging stock up to and including 10 mm thickness/diameter must develop: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 380 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 430 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 9 percent.

Extruded forging stock over 10 mm and up to and including 20 mm must meet: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 400 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 430 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 9 percent.

Extruded forging stock over 20 mm and up to and including 75 mm must meet: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 420 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 460 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 9 percent.

Extruded forging stock over 75 mm and up to and including 150 mm must meet: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 390 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 430 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 9 percent.

Extruded forging stock over 150 mm and up to and including 200 mm must meet: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 350 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 400 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 9 percent.

Forgings of all sizes prepared from cast billets, hot-rolled plates, or extruded stocks must develop: a) 0.2% Proof Stress: minimum 395 MPa; b) Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS): minimum 420 MPa; c) Elongation: minimum 6 percent.

Even if the material satisfies chemical and mechanical tension tests, it must be rejected if faults in manufacturing are detected or if dimensional tolerances, hardness, and metallurgical structures do not comply.

Unless otherwise agreed, each package for dispatch must contain only one size, alloy, and temper of material, and must be permanently marked with the batch/lot number, manufacture date, grade (Alloy 24345), and the manufacturer's trademark.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 7902 : 2001 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing aluminium-copper-magnesium-silicon-manganese alloy (Alloy 24345, equivalent to international grade 2014) forging stocks and forgings used to fabricate structural parts and fittings in the aircraft and aerospace industry [1, 2]. Under India's statutory Aluminium Quality Control Order (QCO), all such forging stocks (including billets, bars, and sections) supplied domestically must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It outlines strict chemical boundaries and heat-treatment procedures (solution treatment and artificial aging) to ensure high structural reliability [2]. The standard enforces detailed mechanical property limits—including a minimum 0.2% proof stress of 350 to 420 MPa depending on the sectional thickness [8]—along with strict retest and manufacturing defect rejections to guarantee safety under high mechanical stress [6].
